interest: For historians, this file provides a compelling window into the twilight of Axis diplomatic and intelligence maneuvers in neutral Spain during the final months of World War II. It illustrates how Japanese Minister Yakichiro Suma clung to unrealistic geopolitical scenarios—such as a separate German-Soviet peace incorporating communism and the renewal of the Soviet-Japanese neutrality pact—even as Allied bombing ravaged Tokyo and the Pacific theater collapsed. Crucially, the file documents the diplomatic crisis triggered by Japanese atrocities against Spanish nationals at the Spanish Consulate General during the Battle of Manila in February 1945, showing Suma's desperate attempts to leverage Soviet diplomatic exclusion to prevent Franco's regime from severing relations. Additionally, the OSS counterintelligence reviews of Japanese press conduits (such as Yomiuri-Hochi correspondent Kuninosuke Matsuo) and post-war surveillance of legation secretary Fumio Miura highlight the joint State Department and OSS apparatus tracking Axis networks across the Iberian Peninsula.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.20252) documents U.S. surveillance and intelligence assessments of Japanese diplomatic, military, and espionage activities in Spain between January 1945 and May 1946. Centered on communications from the American Embassy in Madrid to the Secretary of State, the records feature extensive intelligence obtained from confidential informants regarding Japanese Minister Yakichiro Suma. The reports detail Suma's assessments of the secret Franco-Soviet treaty, prospects for a separate German-Soviet rapprochement, damage from Allied air raids on Tokyo and the dispersal of Japanese industry underground, Japanese naval intentions, and negotiations in Moscow to preserve the Soviet-Japanese non-aggression pact. The file also chronicles the diplomatic tension following Japanese attacks on the Spanish Consulate General in Manila, OSS evaluations of Japanese propaganda newspapers smuggled through local contacts of Yomiuri-Hochi correspondent Kuninosuke Matsuo, and post-war censorship intercepts concerning former legation espionage officer Fumio Miura.

subfiles.about: Reports intelligence from Japanese Minister Yakichiro Suma regarding secret clauses in the Franco-Soviet pact, potential German-Soviet rapprochement, and impending European political maneuvers.
subfiles.from: Carlton J. H. Hayes (American Embassy, Madrid)
subfiles.summary: Embassy Madrid relays secret intelligence obtained via informant PMP from Japanese Minister Yakichiro Suma. Suma alleged that undisclosed provisions in the Franco-Soviet pact granted Russia air and naval bases in Southern France and North Africa, while barring France from independent agreements with Great Britain. He also argued that Germany's Ardennes offensive aimed to gain time to conclude peace with Stalin and institute German communism, establishing an anti-Western bloc aligned with Japan.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-10 from Embassy Madrid on Suma's Remarks Concerning Franco-Russian Agreement and German-Soviet Peace Prospects

subfiles.about: Instructs Embassy Madrid to repeat its secret airgram A-10 regarding Suma's claims to the U.S. diplomatic missions in Paris and Tangier.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Acting Secretary of State [Joseph C. Grew])
subfiles.summary: The Department of State instructs the American Embassy in Madrid to repeat its secret airgram A-10 of January 8, 1945, to U.S. diplomatic missions in Paris and Tangier. This action reflects State Department interest in circulating Suma's assertions regarding French-Soviet agreements and base rights in France and North Africa to the relevant regional posts. The outgoing telegram was filed under decimal file 894.20252/1-845.
subfiles.title: State Department Telegram No. 161 Instructing Madrid to Repeat Airgram A-10 to Paris and Tangier

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording intelligence material concerning Heinrich Bauer filed under decimal file 862.20252/1-1245.
subfiles.summary: A standard State Department cross-reference file note referencing intelligence material concerning 'PEP' and Heinrich Bauer. The underlying document, dated January 12, 1945, is located in decimal file 862.20252/1-1245 (German espionage/military affairs) and cross-filed under 894.20252 due to its bearing on Axis intelligence activities.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Intelligence Material Transmitted Concerning Heinrich Bauer

subfiles.about: Reports Japanese Minister Suma's growing anxiety over American advances in the Pacific and Japanese efforts to remodel its aviation equipment.
subfiles.from: Carlton J. H. Hayes (American Embassy, Madrid)
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Hayes relays brief intelligence from the same Embassy informant regarding Japanese Minister Yakichiro Suma. The informant reported that Suma exhibited notable anxiety regarding the rapid American advance across the Pacific theater. In response to these reverses, Suma stated that Japan was thoroughly altering and reorganizing its military aircraft equipment.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-21 from Embassy Madrid on Suma's Concern Over Pacific Advances and Japanese Aviation Reorganization

subfiles.about: Transmits a Japanese newspaper obtained by an Embassy informant from a Spanish contact employed by Japanese correspondent Kuninosuke Matsuo.
subfiles.from: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim (American Embassy, Madrid)
subfiles.summary: The U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Madrid transmits an enclosed Japanese-language newspaper procured by confidential agent 'X' from Fermin Sanchez, a Spaniard employed by Kuninosuke Matsuo, the Madrid correspondent for Yomiuri-Hochi. The despatch references the Embassy's ongoing 'X-Y' counter-espionage reporting series and forwards the newspaper to Washington for Ozalid reproduction and analysis. This despatch highlights American surveillance of Japanese intelligence operatives using journalistic cover in Spain.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4142 from Embassy Madrid Transmitting Japanese Newspaper Obtained Through Legation Contact

subfiles.about: Returns the copy and translations of the Japanese newspaper Baibai Hochi, concluding it holds no immediate intelligence value.
subfiles.from: Bernard A. Towell, X-2 Branch, Office of Strategic Services (OSS)
subfiles.summary: Bernard A. Towell of the OSS Counterintelligence Branch (X-2) returns the October 20, 1943 issue of 'Baibai Hochi' along with requested English headline translations to Clifton P. English at the Department of State. Towell advises that the newspaper contains no information of current intelligence significance, pointing out that major stories—such as Subhas Chandra Bose establishing the Provisional Indian Government in Singapore—had already been publicized by Domei and other media at the time.
subfiles.title: OSS Memorandum from Bernard A. Towell Returning Japanese Newspaper and Translations to State Department
subfiles.to: Clifton P. English, Department of State

subfiles.about: Provides English translations of the front-page headlines of the October 20, 1943 issue of the Japanese newspaper Baibai Hochi.
subfiles.summary: This document sets out the OSS translation of the primary front-page headlines from the October 20, 1943 issue (No. 23,986) of the Japanese trade newspaper Baibai Hochi. Headlined stories include Japanese Army aviation operations in China, the war death of Lieutenant General Nakazono, administrative reorganizations on the home front, and combat reports from Burma. It also highlights Subhas Chandra Bose's establishment of the Provisional Indian Government in Singapore and its declaration of war against the United States and Great Britain.
subfiles.title: OSS Translation of First Page Headlines from Baibai Hochi of October 20, 1943
subfiles.to: Clifton P. English, Department of State

subfiles.about: A printed Japanese newspaper issue of the Baibai Hochi (Yomiuri-Hochi) dated October 20, 1943, acquired by U.S. intelligence in Spain.
subfiles.summary: Four printed pages of the October 20, 1943 issue of the Japanese daily newspaper Baibai Hochi (associated with the Yomiuri-Hochi publishing group), transmitted as an enclosure to Despatch No. 4142. The paper covers Japanese military operations in the South Pacific, Burma, and China, domestic industrial production drives, and foreign affairs including Indian independence leader Subhas Chandra Bose in Singapore. The text reflects wartime Japanese layout and state-censored news coverage.
subfiles.title: Japanese Newspaper Issue of Baibai Hochi / Yomiuri-Hochi, October 20, 1943

subfiles.about: Reports statements by Japanese Minister Suma on Tokyo air raid destruction, underground industrial relocation, naval strategy, and Soviet-Japanese diplomatic talks.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires W. Walton Butterworth relays detailed remarks made by Japanese Minister Yakichiro Suma to an Embassy informant. Suma claimed that recent Allied air raids had destroyed 10,000 homes in Tokyo but spared central commercial districts, while vital factories along the Tokyo-Yokohama corridor were operating underground. Suma asserted that the Japanese fleet was awaiting an overconfident U.S. advance to launch a decisive attack, dismissed the likelihood of a Soviet attack as utopian, and expressed confidence that Ambassador Naotake Sato would successfully renegotiate the neutrality pact in Moscow.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-143 from Embassy Madrid on Suma's Remarks on Tokyo Bombings, Military Readiness, and Soviet Talks

subfiles.about: Reports Suma's statements regarding escalating Tokyo bombings, underground production, and Soviet diplomatic repercussions if Spain breaks relations over the Manila consulate attack.
subfiles.summary: Embassy Madrid reports further intelligence from Minister Suma regarding increased bombing of Tokyo, with Suma reiterating that factory relocation underground mitigated the damage and that the navy remained poised to attack. Discussing the imminent Spanish public disclosure of the Japanese attack on the Spanish Consulate General in Manila, Suma warned that if Spain severed diplomatic ties, the Soviet Union would react unfavorably to Spanish pro-Allied alignment and work to exclude Spain from future international peace conferences.
subfiles.title: Secret Airgram from Embassy Madrid on Tokyo Bombings, Soviet Geopolitics, and Spanish-Japanese Tensions over Manila

subfiles.about: Transmits an intercepted Japanese letter sent from Kobe to former legation First Secretary Fumio Miura, who had engaged in espionage in Spain.
subfiles.from: Chargé d'Affaires ad interim (American Embassy, Madrid)
subfiles.summary: The American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Madrid transmits an intercepted Japanese-language letter sent from Kobe to Fumio Miura, former First Secretary of the Japanese Legation in Madrid. The cover despatch notes that Miura had been active in Japanese espionage operations during the war and that the letter had recently cleared postal censorship. The Embassy forwards the correspondence for examination by intelligence authorities.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1914 from Embassy Madrid Transmitting Intercepted Japanese Letter Addressed to Fumio Miura

subfiles.about: An intercepted Japanese letter sent from Kobe to former Japanese diplomat and espionage operative Fumio Miura in Madrid.
subfiles.summary: The intercepted Japanese correspondence enclosed with Despatch No. 1914, addressed from Shin'en-dori (Shian-dori), Kobe, Japan, to former First Secretary Fumio Miura of the Japanese Legation in Madrid. Released by Allied occupation censorship in early 1946, the letter reflects post-war monitoring of former Axis diplomatic and intelligence personnel remaining in Spain after the cessation of hostilities.
subfiles.title: Intercepted Japanese Letter Addressed to Former Legation First Secretary Fumio Miura
